get.description: Ascending priority, which is evaluation order — the list reads as the cascade runs.

post.description:
The shipped packs in `db/seeds/rules/`, loaded once per household as `seed` rules.

This exists because `POST /rules` refuses to set `origin` and must keep refusing: a rule
the owner writes in Settings is `user_created`, and a body that could claim otherwise
would put itself in the wrong half of the cascade and lie about where it came from.
`origin` is decided by what did the writing, and this route is that writer.

One pack is one transaction. A slug nothing answers to refuses the whole load rather than
leaving the rules before it behind, because half a pack is a cascade nobody designed.

schema.title: Response Load Pack Rules Pack Post

patch.description:
A full replacement of the editable fields. `origin` and the counters are not editable:
a rule that could rewrite its own provenance could claim to be a seed rule.

delete.description:
Refused while any row names it, by V19's `RESTRICT`. A rule that classified something is
that row's provenance (I6), and deactivating is how such a rule is retired.

post.description: What a candidate rule would match, before it exists. Writes nothing.

Run the cascade over the rows that have no answer, and over nothing else.

This can only fill a row that is `unclassified`. It can never overwrite `user_manual`,
`user_rule`, `merchant_alias`, `prior_match` or `seed_rule` — rules never silently change
past data — and it never runs as a side effect of creating or editing a rule. Re-applying a
rule over rows that already have an answer is Phase 2's learn-from-correction.

V14's `commit_import_batch`, and nothing else.

Every rule about what may commit lives in that function, because the insert and the balance
verification have to share one transaction (`api-contracts.html` §3). This route resolves
the identity, calls it once, and translates its refusals — it does not re-implement any of
them, which is how the two would drift.

Abandon a staged batch, and take its staged rows with it.

Not a reversal. A batch that never committed has nothing in the ledger to undo, and one that
has committed cannot be cancelled at all. What this recovers is the **period**:
`pipeline._refuse_second_staging` already counts `cancelled` among the states that can no
longer commit, so an abandoned batch stops blocking its account's period the moment this
runs. Before it existed there was no way to reach that state from the app, which is how the
slice 1.1 acceptance run found a period blocked for good.

**The staged rows are deleted rather than left carrying a status.** V7's
`reporting_pair_is_locked()` discovers every table with `amount_base` beside `household_id`
and counts rows, and `staged_transaction` has both (V13 says so in its own comment) — so
rows left behind by a batch that can never commit would answer that question `true` for
ever. It bites during onboarding, where the pair is still meant to be changeable: stage a
batch, notice the pair is wrong, cancel, and otherwise still be unable to change it.

What this does **not** free is the file. `idx_document_checksum` is a separate guard, and the
same bytes are still refused on re-upload naming a batch that never imported anything. That
is layer 1's semantics rather than this route's, and is recorded in
`docs/superpowers/progress.md` rather than fixed here.

AccountGroupTotal.title: AccountGroupTotal
AccountGroupTotal.description:
Computed by Postgres. Native per currency: an untagged converted total would be a dated
position without its date.

AccountUpdate.title: AccountUpdate
AccountUpdate.description:
Every editable field, always sent: a full replacement has no absent-versus-null ambiguity
and the client always holds the whole row. Spec C2 requires type, currency, country, the
opening anchor and credit limit to be correctable; account_class stays trigger-derived.

CancelResult.title: CancelResult
CancelResult.description:
What cancelling did. `rowsDiscarded` is stated because the deletion is the point.

A screen that said only "cancelled" would leave the owner unable to tell a batch whose rows
were discarded from one that had none to discard.

CategoryUpdate.title: CategoryUpdate
CategoryUpdate.description:
Always sent in full. Name changes apply to the household's own rows; bucket and
activity apply to any row, because both are stated to be the owner's defaults.

ClassifyResult.title: ClassifyResult
ClassifyResult.description:
`preview=true` reports what would change and writes nothing; otherwise `changed` is what
did. `considered` is every row with no answer, so a small `changed` reads as "the rules do
not cover these yet" rather than as a failure.

LayoutCreate.title: LayoutCreate
LayoutCreate.description:
POST /layouts body. Validation the database cannot express — everything the has_a_balance
anchor CHECK and the sign_convention/chronological_order enums leave uncovered.

LayoutDraft.title: LayoutDraft
LayoutDraft.description: Unsaved layout proposal using the public layout API's field names.

LayoutProposal.title: LayoutProposal
LayoutProposal.description: POST /layouts/propose response. Task 5 later adds normalized preview and reconciliation.

MatchedRow.title: MatchedRow
MatchedRow.description: One row a rule would touch. Money is a string; nothing here computes with it.

PackRule.title: PackRule
PackRule.description:
A rule as a pack file writes it. The one addition is `setCategorySlug`: a pack cannot
carry a category id, because V9 generates a different one in every database, so it names
the slug and the load resolves it (`db/seeds/README.md`).

ParseFailure.title: ParseFailure
ParseFailure.description: A line that extracted and would not normalize. The panel shows these beside the rows.

ParsePeriod.title: ParsePeriod
ParsePeriod.description:
`isDerived` travels with the dates because a derived period must never be read as a
stated one (Invariant I7).

ParseRow.title: ParseRow
ParseRow.description: One normalized row, as the preview and the diagnostics panel read it.

ProposedRawRow.title: ProposedRawRow
ProposedRawRow.description: Public raw extraction row. Sensitive transient extraction fields are absent by design.

Reconciliation.title: Reconciliation
Reconciliation.description:
`reconcile.Verdict` on the wire. Every figure is a string; TypeScript does no arithmetic.

On a `running_balance_break` the three closing fields are row-level rather than
statement-level, so a consumer must read `status` first — the same warning the dataclass
carries, restated here because this is the shape the panel actually receives.

ReviewGroup.title: ReviewGroup
ReviewGroup.description:
Rows sharing a status, and how many there are.

`statement-ingestion.html` §10 groups by attention needed rather than chronologically:
chronological order means scrolling past the rows that are fine to reach the ones that are
not. `count` is stated rather than left to the array's length because a later page of a
large group will not carry every row.

ReviewPeriod.title: ReviewPeriod
ReviewPeriod.description:
The period as `import_batch` recorded it, which is not always all of it.

Every field is optional because every underlying column is. `period_start` and `period_end`
are nullable (V12), so a batch that failed before reconciliation has no period at all and
must still be readable — a review screen that 500s on the batch the owner needs to look at
is the wrong failure. `isDerived` is the flag the batch recorded at staging (V17): true
where the period came from the rows' own dates, false where the statement stated it, and
null only for a batch staged before that column existed. It is never inferred — a period
derived from rows dated 1 and 2 March is indistinguishable afterwards from one a statement
stated as 1-2 March, and guessing either way labels a provenance nobody observed
(Invariant I7).

ReviewRow.title: ReviewRow
ReviewRow.description:
One staged row as the review screen reads it.

Money is a string and the frozen pair travels with the row: the screen shows what will be
written, not a figure it recomputes (`api-contracts.html` §6).

RowDecision.title: RowDecision
RowDecision.description: A bulk decision. Reviewing 200 rows one at a time is why people abandon these tools.

RuleBody.title: RuleBody
RuleBody.description:
Everything a rule can say. Sent in full on create and on edit, as `AccountUpdate` is:
a full replacement has no absent-versus-null ambiguity and the screen holds the whole row.

RuleRow.title: RuleRow
RuleRow.description:
A saved rule. `origin` and the counters are read-only: the first is set by whichever
path created the rule, and the second two are the cascade's to maintain.

TransactionUpdate.title: TransactionUpdate
TransactionUpdate.description:
The two owner-editable fields, always sent — omitting notes would silently erase an
existing note, so it is required and an explicit null is the deliberate clear. Money is
immutable (I1/I5); the database trigger enforces what this model does not offer.
